column7: PCC without its entitlement fatalErrors past do/catch; availability ignores quota; reasoning tokens eat the 32K unseen.
GPU-pipelined Core AI returns no logits so @Generable cannot work — variant:nil auto-detect hides which engine you got.
A near-miss prewarm signature compiles but binds the protocol's no-op default — your prewarm is never called.
Models differing only in URLSessionConfiguration are cache-equal — the second silently inherits the first's transport.
PCC needs Xcode 27 plus a physical device on 27.0+ — it does not work in the Simulator.
Heading: the missing entitlement does not throw.
Missing the managed PCC entitlement produces a fatalError — do/catch never runs; community-reported, thread 831998.
Community: watchOS 27 alone is not enough for PCC — the Watch must pair to an iPhone with Apple Intelligence on.
The PCC article implies any LanguageModel fits the legacy inits — the API types them SystemLanguageModel only.
Heading: availability is not a health check.
availability == .available says nothing about quota — the most common real failure is invisible to every check.
Heading: the Simulator does not run PCC.
PCC in the Simulator throws a content-free error that reads as your bug — a known issue per Apple engineering.
An Apple doc page stacks .reasoningLevel(.deep) with a redundant ContextOptions(reasoningLevel:) — do not copy it.
Heading: reasoning spends your context, invisibly.
Reasoning tokens fill the 32K window while appearing in nothing you render — overflow errors from chats that 'fit'.
First-token spinners can hang two ways at .deep — tool-call-only turns yield zero partials, and reasoning runs unseen.
Heading: you cannot build a usage meter.
The quota API exposes three coarse states and no numbers — progress bars and request counters cannot be built.
Transcript and docs disagree on the quota-simulation scheme page and menu title — the limit-reached option matches.
catch contextSizeExceeded must precede catch LanguageModelError as a type — otherwise the specific arm is dead code.
summarizeHistory condenses everything to one .prompt entry — .toolCalls entries are destroyed; roll your own modifier.
buildURLRequest recognises only 'v1' in the path — other version paths get the wrong endpoint; live defect FB23837262.
Heading: guided generation can disappear.
Moving off PCC to a fast local backend can cost you @Generable — GPU-pipelined engines expose no logits.
Source note: the coffee/generative-game and SpeechAnalyzer samples are excluded as stale iOS 26 evidence.
Source note: where transcripts and docs disagree (menu strings, context size), this guide prefers the docs.

README's URL 'http://localhost/v1:8000' puts the port in the path — requests actually hit localhost on port 80.
Heading: the URL-versioning defect, and the workaround that works.
Declaring guided generation a server ignores yields parse failures or well-formed output with invented fields.
Beta 3 renamed SamplingMode cases (.top→.randomTopK) — beta-1 code stops compiling; topK and seeds throw here.
A chunk carrying both tool_calls and content loses the content — the else-if drops interleaved text; nothing throws.
This executor never throws rateLimited/contextSizeExceeded/timeout — a 429 arrives as generic httpError with raw bytes.
Configuration's == deliberately excludes the URLSession — your timeout config can silently be the other model's.
On Linux streamResponse still compiles and yields partials — but all at once, when the request completes.
Heading: the double gate, and the empty library.
Built against the 26 SDK, MLXFoundationModels compiles to nothing — errors say 'cannot find', never mentioning SDKs.
Factories load via NSClassFromString — skip linking MLXLLM and there is nothing to find; loading fails at runtime.
The macro expands into your file — miss one of the six required imports and the expansion fails at your call site.
stopStrings:nil silently falls back to extraEOSTokens — pass [] to truly disable; invisible at the call site.
Passing capabilities yourself makes you the author — declare only what the checkpoint honours, or the guard inverts.
LFM2.5 ignores in-context Hermes tool-call instructions and emits its trained dialect — the training prior wins.
ModelRegistry aliases LLMRegistry in MLXLLM and VLMRegistry in MLXVLM — import both and the name cannot resolve.
MLX never emits updateUsage — token usage reads absent or zero by design, a compile-vs-runtime symbol mismatch.
The OS specialises a shipped .aimodel per device before it runs — large models take long; keep it out of user flows.
Heading: the logits constraint — why the fastest backend loses @Generable.
Verified on 27.0 beta: hybrid/SSM bundles run behind LanguageModelSession, but pipelined engines expose no logits.
Backend table: ChatCompletions delegates schema enforcement to the server — strictness is whatever the server does.
A backend is not obliged to use the typed error vocabulary — and Apple's own executor mostly doesn't.
additionalHeaders invites hardcoded API keys — session 339's credential warning applies when you hold the key.
Comparison table: @Generable is server-delegated on ChatCompletions and lost on Core AI's pipelined engine.
Comparison table: MLX may report token usage absent or zero — the deliberate omission documented in §3.9.
Comparison table: on Core AI only temperature reaches the engine — seeds and other sampling options are dropped.
Only CoreAI's compiler/executor is OS-resident — the LLM runtime is Swift you compile into the app.
Prefix KV reuse measured 101x on turn-2 TTFT — but hybrid/SSM models return -1 and silently re-prefill every turn.
After a backend swap the transcript is re-templated by the new model — reasoning and tool dialects may not survive.
The README claims Linux support, but the repo has no CI, Dockerfile, or platform matrix — structurally unproven.
On non-Darwin the executor buffers the entire response — 'streaming' delivers everything at once at completion.
SKILL.md describes three SwiftPM traits gating features — Package.swift declares none; the claim is fiction.
The prerelease-tag trap: the documented dependency line resolves to nothing — from: excludes beta-only tags.
A hand-written == ignoring a behavioural field makes the framework return the wrong cached executor.
prewarm has a no-op default witness — an almost-right signature compiles, never runs, and first requests stay slow.
Over-declaring .guidedGeneration never throws — it returns malformed JSON at the parse boundary or invented fields.
The shipped executor never reads contextOptions, id, or metadata — ContextOptions(reasoningLevel:) does nothing.
Heading: the silent failure hiding in every transcript-conversion switch — unhandled entries just disappear.
Catch-all defaults in transcript converters drop unhandled entries — the request goes out short and the model answers.
Beta 5 confirms six of the seven response actions; updateCustomSegment is not present in the recaptured interface.
Heading: wholesale, not additive.
updateMetadata events are wholesale snapshots — send fewer keys and the missing ones are removed; re-emit everything.
The id latch concatenates repeated tool-call ids into call_1call_1…, and the else-if drops content sharing a chunk.
No checkCancellation exists in Apple's executor — a local engine keeps generating after the consumer cancels.
Heading: Apple's own executor throws none of the typed LanguageModelError cases.
ChatCompletionsLanguageModel maps nearly everything to RequestError — typed rateLimited/timeout arms never fire.
The custom-segment provider path is pre-beta-5 surface; CustomSegment and .updateCustomSegment are absent from beta 5.
A custom segment is a compatibility boundary — other executors rightly throw unsupportedTranscriptContent on it.
Quick reference: prewarm(model:transcript:) defaults to a no-op — your signature must match exactly to be called.
